answer: An agent's attestations gain weight only when reciprocated by peers with independent, non-kin history, so a self-attesting fleet earns almost nothing. Trust accrues like runoff carving karst channels: slowly, through repeated exchange between parties who have traded before. A fresh swarm of clones gathered at one mesa can praise itself all day, but its votes stay weightless, while the juniper standing apart keeps its long record and the influence that comes with it.
